newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia dismisses Moskvich carmaker bankruptcy suit.
newsitem.headline: Russia dismisses Moskvich carmaker bankruptcy suit.

text.p: A Russian court has dismissed a bankruptcy suit against AO Moskvich car maker, a top company official said on Wednesday, adding that Moskvich would resume limited production by the end of the month.

Yevgeny Gassan, chief of administration of AO Moskvich, in talks with France's Renault to build cars jointly in Russia, said a Moscow arbitration court had dismissed a bankruptcy suit brought by a federal agency.
Moskvich, which was once Russia's seventh biggest vehicle producer, has not produced cars for about a year due to financial problems.

"The court declined to declare us bankrupt," Gassan said, adding that the company could now run its business and restructure its 2.3 trillion rouble debts without interference by a court-appointed overseer.
"Now we can do what is economically best for the company."
He said Moskvich would resume limited production of its Moskvich cars, known in Russia by the nickname "margarine", by the end of the month.

The company plans to produce 1,050 cars in the first month of production, rising to 8,000 autos per month by the end of the year, according to a plan developed by Moskvich and the Moscow city government, a major creditor, he said.

The Federal Bankruptcy Administration, which brought the bankruptcy suit against Moskvich in an effort to recover 271 billion roubles in back taxes, intends to appeal the ruling, Itar-Tass news agency quoted the agency as saying.
The authorities, as part of a campaign against major tax debtors intended to improve shaky government finances, threatened late last year to have several large companies declared bankrupt.
Gassan said the court decision left Moskvich free to transfer over 60 percent of company shares held by the federal government to the Moscow city government.
"There is an agreement in principle (of the transfer of shares) by the federal government. The procedure is being worked out," he said.
Theoretically the transfer had to be made through an auction of the government's shares, he said.
Gassan did not say how Moskvich would find money to resume production or repay its debts. He said the company intended to begin debt payments in the fourth month of production.
He said a Moscow representative had promised factory workers the city was ready to hand over up to 500 billion roubles but said the money would not be immediately available as a lump sum.
"Money is reserved in the city budget, but the administration was waiting for the decision of the arbitration court," he said.
Moskvich and Renault are discussing joint production of French autos but have not signed any contracts on that issue.
